_comment: ADR-0079 store-occupancy pins (#1428), consumed by bench/store_sweep_gate.py. MEASURED values, never round ceilings — a pin left above the truth makes the next growth free. Re-pin ONLY by a deliberate PR edit: STORE_SWEEP_SCOPE=deterministic bash bench/run_store_sweep.sh bench/build 13 2 > sweep.tsv && python3 bench/store_sweep_gate.py gate --sweep-raw sweep.tsv --pins bench/store_sweep_pins.json --emit-pins
_instrument: bench_store_sweep hwm — per-store pool_source_t::used() after kHwmOpsPerLane full-workload iterations on each of T lanes, summed per (arm, T). The mode runs SINGLE-THREADED over all T lanes on purpose: concurrent draws overlap, which would make the high-water a function of the scheduler. H-baseline is deliberately unpinned — it injects no store, so it has no occupancy; its cost is the escape column, which is never gated.
_measured_spread: Byte-identical across EIGHT invocations on 2026-08-20 (g++ 13.3.0, Release, pinned cpu2): five taken at a 1-minute load average of 32.7 and three at 4.2-4.9. Every one of the 18 (arm, T) cells matched exactly — 0 B, 0.00%, and the store COUNT matched too. That is the column being deterministic by construction rather than merely quiet, which is what earns it a zero-width band.
_band_rationale: ZERO, and deliberately unlike bench/ram_census_pins.json's 8 B. That file's figures come from the process allocator, where a size-class flip can move a number without any design change; these come from libtracer's own pool_source_t over a slab the bench sizes, with no libc allocator in the path, and they were measured byte-identical over eight invocations spanning an 8x range of host load. A tolerance here would not absorb noise there is none of — it would only make the first N bytes of the next growth free. Cross-TOOLCHAIN differences (the std::pmr control blocks carry libstdc++ sizeofs) are handled by the toolchain downgrade below, not by a band, because an unattributable difference must be reported and never enforced.
_toolchain: These figures contain the sizeof of the std::pmr control blocks and of the per-lane store headers, so they are compiler-bound. Measured on a different toolchain than the pin, store_sweep_gate.py reports the drift and enforces in warn mode only (ram_census.effective_mode, imported rather than re-derived).

_never_gated.throughput: RESULT_STORE_TPUT, the fan-out T-sweep at T >= 2. Thread-contention numbers are runner-dependent, and the standing in-tree call for exactly this shape is DIAGNOSTIC-not-gated: bench_rx_source_topology and bench_fanout_clone_storm both decline the gate on that ground. The unpinned throughput window's own A/A null in the #941 banked run read 58.9%. A gate with a 58.9% null is a flaky red, and a flaky red teaches everyone to ignore the gate.
_never_gated.escape: RESULT_STORE_ESCAPE, the process-heap high-water. bench/ram_census_pins.json records a tcp-server hw_peak moving 66% across runs and ~41 KB within one, which is why ram_census.py already excludes high-water columns from its pinned rows. The same caution applies here by construction.
_never_gated.enforcement: Not left to prose. store_sweep_gate.py FAILS on a pin naming any metric outside its GATEABLE list, counts and announces every excluded row it reads, and STORE_SWEEP_SCOPE=deterministic does not run those two arms at all.

_latency_is_banked_not_pinned: The T=1 latency cell of each (arm, leg) IS banked into the perf-local series and IS watched — by store_guard.py drift, against a rolling best-of-window baseline with the range guard, which is this repo's instrument for a timed series. It is deliberately absent from the pins below: measured best-of-13-rounds-x-2-tags over three consecutive windows on 2026-08-20, the worst cross-run spread on any cell was 1.19% and the same-window A/A null band read 1.30 / 1.46 / 2.03%. An exact pin against a column with a ~1-2% floor would red on the host rather than on the code; a band wide enough to be safe would be wider than most regressions worth catching.

activation.criterion: Flip perf-local.yml's `--mode warn` to `--mode fail` once 20 consecutive pinned-host samples have been banked with no unexplained STORE_SWEEP_GATE warning AND ADR-0079 Stage 2 (#843) has either landed and been re-pinned or is known not to be landing inside the window. 20 points is about a release's worth of main pushes here — the same evidence bar bench/ram_census_pins.json set before its own flip. Until then a threshold picked before the noise is known is the unreachable-budget failure mode this repo already hit once.
activation.flipped: FLIPPED to `--mode fail` by #2414. The noise question the criterion waits on is answered: 375 banked bench-local transcripts from 2026-08-20 to 2026-11-08 change only at the sixteen merges listed in `_repin_2414`, and three fresh invocations on 2026-11-08 were byte-identical. What warn mode did NOT do is stop growth: the pins went stale by 22,944 B at NARROW T=24 and nobody saw it (#2406). A cross-toolchain run still downgrades to warn (`_toolchain`).
activation.stage2_step: PRE-DECLARED, so the series does not flag the fix as the regression. ADR-0079 Stage 2 (#843, gated on #1285) moves vertex placement off the global heap (`std::make_unique<vertex_t>`) onto the injected store. Every `used_total` pin below will then STEP UP by the vertex population's worth, and NARROW's `stores` count may change with it. The correct response in that PR is a re-pin from a fresh transcript (`--emit-pins`), quoted in the PR body, NEVER a widened band: the step is the deliverable being priced, and pricing it is the whole reason this series exists. The ratchet ships warn-first partly so that PR cannot be reddened by the very growth it was written to buy.

_repin_2414: Re-pinned 2026-11-08 (#2414) at main 3f0def32f, from three byte-identical deterministic invocations (g++ 13.3.0, Release). The pins had not moved since #1439 banked them; every change since is attributed by the bench-local transcript of each first-parent merge, and by a core-only backfill build for #2329, whose own point failed calibration until #2407 fixed the bench (#2407 itself moves no used() figure). Deltas as T=1 / T=24 used_total on WIDE, MID, NARROW: #1574 graph_t on one injected source +192/+192, +200/+200, +200/+200; #1575 child_registry_t chunks on an injected source +336/+4032 on all three; #1576 try_reserve on the injected source +256/+256, +240/+240, +240/+240; #1578 one block per source-backed segment +88/+88; #1639 value_t replaces the LKV wrapper -192/-1664, -176/-1648, -176/-1648; #1882 graph core on the allocation seam +1920/+12928, +1904/+12912, +1904/+12912; #1892 net plane state on the allocation seam +336/+8832, +336/+8832, +336/+8848; #2058 bus listing draws from the owning graph +208/+208; #2047 one walk, one gate -32/-400; #2059 link needs its connection vertex +176/+5184, +184/+5192, +176/+5184; #2102 router keeps only the link binding -32/-768; #2251 path-label plane deleted -128/-3072; #2282 tenancy word on each link's mount +16/+384; #2346 graph ropes on the arena +192/+192; #2329 no per-request draws for a small terminus reply 0/0, -128/-128, -128/-3072; #2636 (#2413) tenancy pointer on the bus token cache -16/-384. Store counts are unchanged.
